source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1952, p. 10 ("County and rural council nominations")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)

note: Triennial election of the district electoral divisions of Hillsborough rural district, one member each, polled on 5 June 1952. Only Carryduff was contested; two new members were returned unopposed. The other thirteen divisions are recorded from the Returning Officer's notice of result (Lisburn Standard, 6 June 1952, p. 1), which also confirms the Carryduff poll (Booth 352, Carlisle 250) and the Anahilt and Edenderry returns; Drumbo's retiring member was deemed re-elected (meetings pass, 7 Nov 2026). Of Magheraconluce; in place of Mr. John Martin. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Anahilt' to Annahilt (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Hillsborough Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Annahilt; the rounds were filed as Anahilt (1924, 1927, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1952, 1955, 1961, 1964); Annahilt (1930, 1933, 1949, 1958, 1967). This round was filed as 'Anahilt', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (anahilt) answers with a redirect to this one.
